---
title: "DIF, linking and equating"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110)
library(IRTistic)
set.seed(2026)
```

## Screening for DIF with observed-score methods

`dif_test()` gives the classical procedures: Mantel-Haenszel with the ETS
A/B/C classes (Holland & Thayer, 1988), and logistic or ordinal logistic
regression with the Jodoin and Gierl (2001) effect-size classes.

```{r}
n <- 1200
base <- sim_irt(10, 12, "2pl"); tr <- attr(base, "truth")
tr$a[c(5, 9)] <- c(1.3, 1.4); tr$b[c(5, 9), 1] <- c(0, 0.3)   # two well-measured items to study
group <- rep(c("reference", "focal"), n / 2)
theta <- rnorm(n) - 0.4 * (group == "focal")             # the groups differ in ability (impact)
dat <- sim_irt(n, a = tr$a, b = tr$b, model = "2pl", theta = matrix(theta))
f <- group == "focal"
dat$I05[f] <- rbinom(sum(f), 1, plogis(tr$a[5] * (theta[f] - tr$b[5] - 0.9)))   # uniform DIF
dat$I09[f] <- rbinom(sum(f), 1, plogis(0.4 * (theta[f] - tr$b[9])))             # non-uniform DIF

fit <- irt_fit(dat, "2pl")
dif_test(fit, group, method = "lr")
```

## IRT-based DIF with linking and purification

`dif_irt()` calibrates each group separately, links the focal group to the
reference scale by Stocking-Lord on anchor items, and compares the item
parameters with Lord's (1980) Wald test. Items flagged at each round are
removed from the anchor set until it is stable (Candell & Drasgow, 1988).
Effect sizes include Raju's (1988) signed and unsigned areas and Meade's
(2010) SIDS/UIDS, which are expected score differences weighted by the focal
group's ability distribution and so are in score points. Their sum is the
differential test functioning (DTF).

```{r}
res <- dif_irt(fit, group, reference = "reference")
res
```

```{r, fig.height = 4}
plot_dif(res)
plot_dif_curves(res)
```

## Linking two calibrations

```{r}
x <- sim_irt(1000, a = tr$a, b = tr$b, model = "2pl", theta = matrix(rnorm(1000, 0.5, 1.2)))
y <- sim_irt(1000, a = tr$a, b = tr$b, model = "2pl", theta = matrix(rnorm(1000)))
fx <- irt_fit(x[, 1:9], "2pl", se = "none")     # form X: items 1-9
fy <- irt_fit(y[, 4:12], "2pl", se = "none")    # form Y: items 4-12; anchors 4-9
lk <- irt_link(fx, fy, method = "stocking-lord")
lk
```

The true constants are A = 1.2 and B = 0.5. The estimates differ from them by sampling error: two samples of 1,000 and only six anchor items.

## True-score equating and score tables

```{r}
eq <- equate_true_score(lk, fy)
irt_table(eq, digits = 2)
irt_table(score_table(fy), digits = 3)
```
